# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

We only provide security updates for the latest tagged version (by date).

Security issues are only within scope when the software is used in a supported environment and for the intended purpose, and only as long as the issue arises from our code – not the Operating System, not the programming language, not the site or third party service you are connecting to.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

> [!CAUTION]
> Do NOT report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub Issues or any other form of _public_ communication.

Please use GitHub Security Advisories to report vulnerabilities.

1. Go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/grafida/grafida/security/advisories).
2. Click "Report a vulnerability".
3. Fill out the advisory form.

This creates a private discussion visible only to the maintainer.

## Response Timeline

Realistic commitments we can actually meet:

- **Initial response**: Within 4 business days
- **Status update**: Within 14 business days
- **Resolution target**: Within 90 days

Regarding the resolution target, we generally aim for fast resolution, ideally a single-digit number of days. If we propose a timeline which is too short for you, please do tell us.

Kindly note that the resolution target does not include the amount of time it takes Google to review the new version and release it.

### What to do if you do not receive a timely reply.

This project is maintained by a single developer whose availability may be limited due to factors outside his control, such as illness or family obligations. We are unlikely to be out of contact for more than five days.

If you do not receive an initial response within 10 calendar days, please try contacting us again. A simple "Bump" comment on your vulnerability report is enough.

If you do not receive an answer after 30 calendar days, please use [my site's contact page](https://www.dionysopoulos.me/contact-me) to email me asking what's going on.

## Disclosure Policy

- **Coordinated disclosure**: We work with reporters to agree on a disclosure timeline.
- **Credit**: Security reporters are credited in release notes and advisories (unless they prefer anonymity).
- **CVE assignment**: We request CVEs through GitHub for verified vulnerabilities; due to the nature of this process, we may not have a CVE number when we publish a security update.

## Use of generative AI

We find AI-powered code assistants to be very useful development tools, especially in discovering and addressing security issues. However, the very nature of these tools leaves a great margin for error and misuse. If you are using AI to discover and / or report security issues, we ask you to heed our "Statement on the use of AI" linked to from our README.

## Bug Bounty

As a single person with very limited resources, I am unfortunately unable to offer a bug bounty. Security reports are greatly appreciated and credited. Thank you for helping keep everyone safe!
